channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: ReScale4DL: balancing pixel and contextual information for enhanced bioimage segmentation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77930-1

Deep-learning segmentation accuracy depends on image resolution, with each architecture having an optimum, usually at a lower microscopy resolution. Here, the authors present ReScale4DL, a framework for optimising imaging experiments by selecting resolutions to balance accuracy, throughput and cost.
item.dc:title: ReScale4DL: balancing pixel and contextual information for enhanced bioimage segmentation

item.title: Large strain and high reversible dielectric tunability in Sm-modified PMN-PT ceramics
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77914-1

Relaxor ferroelectrics promise adaptive electronics, but strain and reversible tunability are difficult to combine. Zhang et al. tuned titanium content and local polar correlations in a perovskite to balance strong actuation, dielectric agility, and low hysteresis.
item.dc:title: Large strain and high reversible dielectric tunability in Sm-modified PMN-PT ceramics

item.title: Microglia and border-associated macrophages play opposite roles in cerebrovascular and leukocyte responses under systemic inflammation in male mice
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77787-4

How brain myeloid cells regulate vascular responses in systemic inflammation is unclear. Here, the authors identify distinct roles for microglia and border-associated macrophages in leukocyte recruitment and cerebral blood flow regulation via IL-1.
item.dc:title: Microglia and border-associated macrophages play opposite roles in cerebrovascular and leukocyte responses under systemic inflammation in male mice

item.title: Spatiotemporal metabolic networks in a preclinical model of pancreatic cancer and associated cachexia
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77745-0

Cachexia commonly develops in patients with pancreatic cancer and is closely linked to increased morbidity and mortality. Here, the authors provide an in-depth longitudinal characterization of systemic metabolomic alterations in a mouse model of pancreatic cancer–associated cachexia.
item.dc:title: Spatiotemporal metabolic networks in a preclinical model of pancreatic cancer and associated cachexia

item.title: A ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase facilitates H2A.Z removal in response to phosphate starvation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77882-6

Under phosphate starvation, plants undergo transcriptional reprogramming. Here Meng et al. show that the PHR1 transcription factor recruits the UCH2 deubiquitinase to remove ubiquitin from the H2A.Z histone variant at target genes, promoting H2A.Z eviction and activating phosphate starvation responses.
item.dc:title: A ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase facilitates H2A.Z removal in response to phosphate starvation

item.title: Autophagy inhibition sensitizes radiotherapy responses in high-grade mutant IDH1 glioma
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77320-7

Mutations in IDH1 are linked to altered metabolism and increased autophagy in glioma. Here, authors show that inhibiting autophagy sensitizes mutant IDH1 glioma cells to radiation and improves outcomes in preclinical models.
item.dc:title: Autophagy inhibition sensitizes radiotherapy responses in high-grade mutant IDH1 glioma

item.title: Whisker-based tactile flight for tiny drones
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77366-7

Inspired by nocturnal animals that use whiskers to navigate, this study presents a 3-gram tactile sensor enabling tiny drones to detect obstacles by touch, supporting onboard tactile sensing for navigation and exploration in visually challenging environments.
item.dc:title: Whisker-based tactile flight for tiny drones
item.dc:creator: Chaoxiang Ye
Guido de Croon
Salua Hamaza

item.title: Omaveloxolone functions as a molecular crowbar-like degrader of STING to alleviate aging-related inflammation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77760-1

Aging-related inflammation can have excessive activation of the STING pathway as some of its features. Here the authors look at the function of Omaveloxolone and show this compound binds to the base of the STING ligand-binding domain and destabilises STING leading to STING K27-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation and show Omaveloxolone reducing aging associated inflammation in aged male mice.
item.dc:title: Omaveloxolone functions as a molecular crowbar-like degrader of STING to alleviate aging-related inflammation
